final_answer:
Using donor-level PBMC composition across 162 SLE donors and 98 adequately sampled healthy donors (1 control donor with only 456 cells was excluded), the cell populations with significantly altered frequencies in SLE were:

Increased in SLE:
- classical monocyte: mean donor fraction 28.54% in SLE vs 18.22% in controls; BH-adjusted q=9.044e-12.
- lymphocyte: mean donor fraction 0.87% in SLE vs 0.38% in controls; BH-adjusted q=1.329e-07.
- non-classical monocyte: mean donor fraction 4.35% in SLE vs 3.07% in controls; BH-adjusted q=2.200e-03.

Decreased in SLE:
- CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cell: mean donor fraction 24.77% in SLE vs 37.22% in controls; BH-adjusted q=2.912e-13.
- plasmacytoid dendritic cell: mean donor fraction 0.30% in SLE vs 0.57% in controls; BH-adjusted q=2.246e-07.
- B cell: mean donor fraction 12.07% in SLE vs 12.40% in controls; BH-adjusted q=5.198e-03.
- natural killer cell: mean donor fraction 6.94% in SLE vs 7.99% in controls; BH-adjusted q=2.494e-02.
- conventional dendritic cell: mean donor fraction 1.34% in SLE vs 1.53% in controls; BH-adjusted q=3.472e-02.
- progenitor cell: mean donor fraction 0.06% in SLE vs 0.07% in controls; BH-adjusted q=4.751e-02.

The largest broad shifts were an increase in classical monocytes and a decrease in CD4-positive alpha-beta T cells. An exploratory incomplete subtype annotation further suggested depletion of naive CD4 T cells and enrichment of effector-memory/regulatory CD4 subsets in SLE, but the primary answer above is based on the complete broad cell-type labels.

criterion_4.reason: Used Mann-Whitney test and logit-linear model with FDR correction across 11 cell types, properly reporting adjusted p-values.
